from: July book, night 25 (Our Eyes Are on You)
p1: One day King Jehoshaphat heard that a big army was coming. He felt afraid. He asked everyone in Judah to fast: to skip food and pray very hard.
People came from every town to the Lord’s house. There Jehoshaphat prayed for help.
He said, “We do not know what to do. But our eyes are upon You.” They looked to the Lord, like a child looks up to a parent.
p2: All of Judah stood before the Lord with their families, even the little ones. Heavenly Father hears little ones too. Jesus loved little children and blessed them.
When you do not know what to do, look to Heavenly Father together. Tonight, kneel with your family and pray.
old: A huge army was coming to fight King Jehoshaphat’s people. There were so many enemies! Jehoshaphat felt afraid. But he knew exactly what to do — he gathered everyone to pray.
Jehoshaphat prayed a beautiful prayer: “Heavenly Father, we don’t know what to do. But OUR EYES ARE UPON THEE.” That means, “We are looking to You for help, Lord!”

Heavenly Father answered, “Don’t be afraid. This battle is Mine. Just stand still and watch Me save you.” So the next day, the people SANG praises to God as they marched out. And the enemies were defeated without Judah even fighting!
When we don’t know what to do, we can look to Heavenly Father. “Our eyes are upon Thee” means we trust God to lead us. He fights our battles. We just need to keep our eyes on Him.
